checks.question: O2 arithmetic: umol O2 available in the closed vial (air vs O2-flushed) against R2's 250 - 700 umol (air arm) / 500 - 1900 umol (air + Cu arm) and R1's 4 - 8 umol, per 1 mmol pot.
checks.pass_rule: (inventory) Unit umol O2; error the vial volume's print rounding. Under air, R2 is refuted if available O2 < 250 umol. If the headspace is unprinted, the outcome is the headspace-to-liquid ratio each rival needs.
checks.outcome: INCONCLUSIVE on printed data (the headspace is unprinted), but sharpened: R2 needs a headspace / liquid volume ratio r >= 2.9 (air arm, low end) to 8.2 (high end); its copper arm, which footnote c states is AIR, needs r >= 5.8 to 22 whatever the reading of expt II. R1 needs r >= 0.06 (any vial). The O2-flush reading rescues R2's air arm at r >= 0.6 - 1.7 but never its copper arm. At the footnotes' 10 mL scale a common closed vial (<= 30 mL, r <= 2) refutes R2 under air; at the Experimental's 1 mL scale a >= 7 mL vial would not.
evidence: Air at sealing (25 C, 1 atm): 101325 / (8.314 x 298.15) = 40.9 umol gas per mL; x 0.2095 = 8.56 umol O2 per mL headspace. Pure O2: 40.9 umol/mL (4.78x).
Dissolved at sealing: air-saturated water ~0.26 mmol/L (8.3 mg/L, 25 C), pure-O2-saturated ~1.24 mmol/L; 0.5 M phosphate salts out ~10 - 15 % (upper bounds used).
Per mmol precursor (0.1 mmol/mL in every reading): available O2 = 85.6 r + 2.6 umol/mmol under air; 409 r + 12.4 under O2 (r = V_headspace / V_liquid).
R1 (air excess PA + PAA 7.6 umol; Cu 20.5): r >= (7.6 - 2.6) / 85.6 = 0.06; Cu arm r >= 0.21.
Examples: 10 mL in a 20 mL vial r = 1.0 -> 88 umol/mmol (air); 1 mL in a 4 mL vial r = 3 -> 259; 1 mL in a 10 mL vial r = 9 -> 773.

Rate flag (assumption-laden, not a verdict): R2's low end consumes 250 umol per 10 mL in 120 min = 0.21 mmol/L/min. Liquid O2 at 100 C under the sealed air headspace (pO2 ~0.26 atm, solubility ~0.75 mmol/L/atm) is ~0.2 mmol/L, so the vessel would need k_L a >= ~1 /min. Unstirred closed vials typically run 1e-4 - 1e-3 /s (0.006 - 0.06 /min). P(R2's O2 demand is transfer-feasible in an unstirred closed vial) ~0.2 (mine). R1's 0.006 mmol/L/min needs nothing.
